propositions: Rebar must support multiple LLM providers (Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic), VCS platforms (Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab), CI systems (Jenkins), and issue trackers (Jira Cloud/DC) across diverse deployment environments without weakening SDK-native refresh, workload identity, or credential rotation mechanisms.

Static credentials for long-running processes (MCP/server) must rotate via restart/redeploy rather than hot-reload; CLI processes receive current environment at startup; native temporary credentials remain SDK-owned and may refresh in-process.

Operation snapshots must remain structurally non-secret; provider-native credential/session capabilities (boto3 Session, Anthropic AccessTokenProvider, OpenAI workload identity) are injected into Rebar-owned factories; unavoidable static values use Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes only in provider-specific non-serializable containers excluded from fingerprints/caches/serialization.

Subprocess environment inheritance is standard for trusted same-capability children; Rebar overlays materialized static credentials only onto owning children, removes exact Rebar-declared sibling-secret names, and never mutates global os.environ.

Application startup accepts op-cert signing keys via REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (preferred) or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY; deployment resolves external secret stores (SSM, files, mounts) before process startup; no application-owned runtime retrieval, universal secret broker, or built-in keyring adapter is introduced.

Current defect: _bridge_runner copies full parent environment to reconciler and ticket delivery, exposing unrelated provider credentials; must replace with adapter-owned baseline and only selected capabilities per operation.
